correctness.rationale: For the 20-vertex cubic GP(10,2), after deleting k vertices with e(S) internal edges the 20−k complement has 30−3k+e(S) edges. Forest inequality <=19−k implies 11+e(S)<=2k, so every FVS has k>=6. Exact enumeration of all C(20,6)=38,760 six-subsets finds 2,520 valid minima, with 660 e(S)=0 and 1,860 e(S)=1. For each state, the complete token-slide adjacency list is obtained by exchanging a selected vertex for an adjacent unselected vertex and retaining the move exactly when the new mask is in the enumerated optimal set. A fully independent Python reconstruction performed the complete search (not a sample) and all 2,520 BFS distance sweeps: one connected graph, 8,880 edges, stratum edges 1,620/4,140 and crossing 3,120, eccentricities exactly 120 at distance 8, 2,340 at 9, 60 at 10. Therefore radius 8 and sharp diameter 10; stratum connectivity follows the supplied component search. The original two independent programs use DSU vs leaf-pruning and transition detection by moves vs pairwise symmetric differences. Such a complete finite exhaust does prove this one finite statement, but not a general graph-family theorem.

value.rationale: The dodecahedron is a canonical cubic large-girth object and the minimum-feedback-set space is a natural optimization landscape. Connectivity and sharp distances under physically local token slides are mathematically different from known arbitrary-jump connectivity; the full radius/eccentricity/stratum profile is a complete motivated finite classification, not an arbitrary isolated count.

limitations: The theorem concerns only GP(10,2), not all planar cubic graphs.
The all-source BFS is exhaustive for the finite claimed set, unlike a sample; does not prove a structural formula for other graphs.
